'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War on drugs]]
**[[2025 US Caribbean naval deployment]]
***[[United States]] [[U.S. president|president]] [[Donald Trump]] claims that the [[U.S. military]] carried out a strike on an alleged [[Venezuela]]n drug cartel vessel in [[international waters]], killing three people, making it the [[2025 United States strike on Venezuelan boat|second such strike]] carried out against a suspected drug boat in September. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/trump-says-us-struck-another-alleged-venezuelan-drug-vessel-killing-three-2025-09-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[War in the Sahel]]
**[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
***[[Nigeria]]n [[Nigerian Armed Forces|troops]] kill at least eleven [[Islamic State – West Africa Province|ISWAP]] fighters in two operations in the [[Adamawa State|Adamawa]] and [[Borno State|Borno]] [[States of Nigeria|states]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/nigerian-military-kills-11-iswap-militants-borno-adamawa-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Haitian conflict (2020–present)|Haitian conflict]]
**Armed [[Haitian conflict (2020–present)#Known gangs and groups|gangs]] attack an [[armored vehicle]] in [[Kenscoff]], [[Haiti]], killing the driver and injuring two [[Haitian National Police|police officers]] on board. [https://apnews.com/article/haiti-gangs-armored-vehicle-kenscoff-labodri-cda2b7718453d9d0ec05e7a4de4cff2a (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Mexico–United States relations]]
**The [[U.S. Department of Transportation]] orders [[Mexico|Mexican]] [[flag carrier]] [[Aeroméxico]] and [[Major airlines of the United States|U.S. major carrier]] [[Delta Air Lines]] to end their [[joint venture]] by January 1, 2026, citing [[Anti-competitive practices|anti-competitive]] effects on Mexico–U.S. routes. [https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/trump-administration-orders-delta-aeromexico-end-joint-venture-by-january-1-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Australia]]n bank [[ANZ (bank)|ANZ]] agrees to pay [[Australian dollar|AU$]]240 million ([[United States dollar|US$]]160 million) in penalties, the largest ever imposed by the [[Australian Securities and Investments Commission|Securities and Investments Commission]], for misconduct including irregularities in a [[government bond]] deal and failures affecting its customers. [https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/australias-anz-pay-160-million-over-bond-deal-customer-violations-2025-09-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Sudanese refugee crisis (2023–present)|Sudanese refugee crisis]]
**At least 50 people are killed after a boat carrying [[Sudan]]ese [[Refugees of Sudan|refugees]] catches fire off the coast of [[Libya]], with 24 survivors receiving medical assistance. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/iom-says-least-50-dead-after-vessel-carrying-sudanese-refugees-caught-fire-off-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*Four people are killed and nine others injured after a bus collides with a truck in [[Uttar Pradesh]], [[India]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/lucknow/uttar-pradesh-crash-4-dead-several-injured-as-tourist-bus-collides-with-truck-in-jaunpur/articleshow/123892651.cms (''The Times of India'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israel–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[United Kingdom and the Gaza war]]
***The [[United Kingdom|British]] [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|defence ministry]] bans [[Israelis]] from attending the [[Royal College of Defence Studies]] over Israel's decision to [[2025 Gaza City offensive|fully invade]] [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/britain-bans-israelis-london-defence-college-over-gaza-escalation-2025-09-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[South Korea–United States relations]]
**[[2025 Georgia Hyundai plant immigration raid]]
***[[South Korea]] announces it will launch a formal investigation into [[human rights in the United States|human rights]] abuses by [[Immigrations and Customs Enforcement|U.S. federal personnel]] during the raid at a [[Hyundai]] factory in [[Georgia (US state)|Georgia]] earlier this month. [https://www.dw.com/en/south-korea-probes-rights-violations-in-us-factory-raid/a-73996953 (DW)]
*[[Colombia–United States relations]], [[Colombian conflict]]
**The [[United States]] adds [[Colombia]] to its list of countries failing to meet [[War on drugs|international counter-narcotics]] obligations for the first time since 1997, citing increased [[cocaine]] [[Illegal drug trade in Colombia|production]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20250916-us-decertifies-colombia-in-drug-war-for-first-time-in-nearly-30-years (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Flood control projects controversy in the Philippines]]
**[[Philippine]] [[President of the Philippines|president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] appoints former [[Supreme Court of the Philippines|Supreme Court]] [[Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the Philippines|associate justice]] [[Andres Reyes Jr.]] as the chairperson of the newly established [[Independent Commission for Infrastructure]] to investigate [[corruption in the Philippines|corruption]] in [[flood control]] projects. [https://www.rappler.com/philippines/former-sc-justice-andres-reyes-jr-chair-independent-commission-infrastructure/ (Rappler)]
*[[Violations of non-combatant airspaces during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Poland]] detains a [[Belarusians in Poland|Belarusian]] woman and a [[Ukrainians in Poland|Ukrainian]] man after a [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|drone]] flew over the [[Presidential Palace, Warsaw|Presidential Palace]] in [[Warsaw]] and was neutralized by the [[State Protection Service]]. [https://apnews.com/article/poland-drone-president-warsaw-ukrainian-belarusian-operators-463525feb87b5bb1e6123d9ed434a5ac (AP)]
*[[India]]'s [[Supreme Court of India|Supreme Court]] clears the [[Vantara]] [[wildlife rescue]] centre, run by the [[Reliance Foundation]], of allegations of [[Wildlife smuggling|illegal animal acquisition]] and [[Cruelty to animals|mistreatment]] after a court-appointed investigation found no such violations. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/indias-top-court-appointed-committee-clears-ambani-sons-wildlife-centre-2025-09-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Recorder of London]] [[Mark Lucraft]] sentences [[English people|English]] couple [[Constance Marten and Mark Gordon]] to 14 years in [[HM Prison Service|prison]] each for the [[Manslaughter in English law#Manslaughter by gross negligence|manslaughter]] of their newborn daughter. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/constance-marten-mark-gordon-sentence-baby-daughter-death/ (CBS News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 deployment of federal forces in the United States]]
**U.S. president [[Donald Trump]] orders the deployment of the [[Army National Guard]] to [[Memphis, Tennessee|Memphis]], [[Tennessee]], to "combat [[Crime in Tennessee|crimes]]". [https://www.the-independent.com/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-memphis-national-guard-crime-b2827096.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[2025 Tanzanian general election]]
**[[Tanzania]]'s [[National Electoral Commission (Tanzania)|electoral commission]] disqualifies [[ACT-Wazalendo]] candidate [[Luhaga Mpina]] from the upcoming [[President of Tanzania|presidential]] election for a second time, reversing its earlier approval on September 13. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tanzania-opposition-presidential-candidate-barred-second-time-2025-09-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Belarus]]ian [[Belarusian opposition|opposition]] politician [[Mikola Statkevich]], released last week as part of a prisoner deal, is returned to a [[penal colony]] in [[Hlybokaye]], [[Vitebsk region]], after refusing deportation to [[Lithuania]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/freed-belarusian-opposition-politician-who-refused-deportation-is-back-prison-2025-09-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Chad]]'s [[National Assembly of Chad|National Assembly]] approves [[Chadian constitution of 2018|constitutional amendments]] extending [[List of heads of state of Chad|presidential]] terms from five to seven years and removing [[term limit]]s, with a final [[Senate of Chad|Senate]] vote scheduled for October 13. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/chad-votes-allow-president-run-unlimited-times-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2025 World Athletics Championships]]
**[[2025 World Athletics Championships – Men's pole vault]]
***[[Swedish Americans|Swedish–American]] [[pole vault]]er [[Armand Duplantis]] breaks his own [[Men's pole vault world record progression|world record]] of 6.29 meters set in 2025 by jumping 6.30 meters, winning him the gold medal at the [[World Athletics Championships]]. [https://www.olympics.com/en/news/mondo-duplantis-world-record-gold-world-athletics-championships-2025-pole-vault (International Olympic Committee)]
*[[2025 Women's Rugby World Cup]]
**In [[rugby union]], [[France women's national rugby union team|France]]'s [[Axelle Berthoumieu]] receives a 12-match suspension for biting [[Ireland women's national rugby union team|Ireland]]'s [[Aoife Wafer]] during their [[Women's Rugby World Cup]] [[2025 Women's Rugby World Cup knockout stage#France vs Ireland|quarterfinal]], while teammate [[Manaé Feleu]] is banned for three matches for a dangerous [[Tackle (football move)|tackle]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/09/16/sport/rugby-womens-world-cup-axelle-berthoumieu-ban-biting-intl (CNN)]
